market_brief: Big AI week: Nvidia reports Tuesday under an interim CEO after Jensen Huang's exit knocked the stock ~13% last week, and Anthropic's IPO is slated to price Wednesday and list Thursday. Even so, US averages posted their best week since August as money rotated within tech. Policy backdrop is hawkish almost everywhere: a hot October CPI keeps a December Fed hike in play, the BoE and RBA have hiked, the BoJ is leaning to a December move, and the RBI is in 'calibrated tightening'. Oil has cooled on US-Iran diplomacy, while crypto and precious metals had a rough week.
ai_brief: A dense release week: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at lower prices, Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to paying users and launched the cheaper Gemini 4 Hydrogen plus a classification-only model, and Thinking Machines open-sourced Inkling 2 Small. Capital-markets attention now shifts to the Anthropic IPO and Nvidia's results as the two big tests of the AI trade.

items.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress steps in as interim CEO
items.summary: Huang left amid scrutiny over ties to a businesswoman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence. NVDA fell ~13% on the week, its worst weekly drop since April 2025, though other chip names rallied.

items.headline: Nvidia reports Tue Nov 17 after the close: Street looks for ~$2.4–2.47 EPS on ~$108.7–108.9B revenue
items.summary: Focus is on guidance, the CEO search, Singapore-linked revenue and any data-centre regulation risk after the Democratic midterm sweep. Yorkville Ives' Dan Ives still expects robust demand metrics.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO: 825M shares at $70–78, Nasdaq ticker ANT; pricing reportedly Nov 18, trading Nov 19
items.summary: Up to ~$64B raised at a fully diluted value of roughly $1.26–1.41T, plus a $26B private placement at the IPO price from AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. Dates are per CNBC sources, not confirmed by the company.

items.headline: US averages log best week since August despite Nvidia slide
items.summary: S&P 500 tech snapped a five-week slump as investors rotated into Apple, AMD and Broadcom rather than leaving the AI trade. Friday itself was soft: Nasdaq -0.9%, S&P -0.4%, Dow +0.1%.

items.headline: US October CPI +0.4% m/m vs 0.3% expected; core +0.3% vs 0.2%
items.summary: No year-on-year rate was published because the 2025 shutdown left no October 2025 base; September's annual rate was 3.7%. The print firmed bets on a December Fed hike.

items.headline: Fed (Warsh) on hold at 3.75–4.00% after September hike; December 8–9 hike priced, minutes due Wed
items.summary: October's 10–2 hold saw Cook and Hammack dissent for a hike. Markets expect hikes to resume in December and continue into 2027 with inflation ~1pt above target.

items.headline: Bank of England hikes to 4.00%, first increase since 2023
items.summary: 8–1 vote with one member for 50bp. The Bank now sees CPI peaking near 5% in mid-2027 on energy costs; markets price roughly even odds of another hike on Dec 17.

items.headline: RBI repo at 5.50% after October hike, stance 'calibrated tightening'; next MPC Dec 2–4
items.summary: The MPC raised the repo rate 25bp on Oct 7 and signalled cuts are off the table near term; it projects FY27 CPI at 5.2% and GDP at 7.1%.

items.headline: BoJ opinions lean hawkish; markets price ~76–85% odds of a December hike from 1.25%
items.summary: Board members broadly agreed the next move is up. The yen barely benefited, with USD/JPY near 158–160, as a simultaneous Fed hike would keep the rate gap intact.

items.headline: RBA lifts cash rate to 4.85%, its fifth hike of 2026; Bank of Canada also hiked to 2.5% in October
items.summary: The global tightening wave triggered by the energy shock continues beyond the Fed and BoE.

items.headline: China extends suspension of extra 24% tariff on US goods, keeps 10% levy
items.summary: Seen as risk-positive ahead of APEC; separately, China's October CPI rose 0.7% y/y, a touch below forecasts.

items.headline: Nifty and Sensex hit highest since February 2026 on FII inflows and easing West Asia tension
items.summary: Banks led the rally (Nifty Bank +11% for the month at that point). DIIs have absorbed most of 2026's foreign selling, buying ~₹7 lakh crore year to date.

items.headline: Crude keeps retreating on US-Iran diplomacy hopes
items.summary: Oil fell sharply on de-escalation headlines through early November, easing some of the energy-driven inflation fear behind global rate hikes. Brent is still up >50% YTD.

items.headline: JPMorgan upgrades SAP to Overweight, PT €275 (from €175): 'no longer priced for AI disruption'
items.summary: Also last week: Citi upgraded Rollins to Buy (PT $49); Rothschild Redburn upgraded American Airlines to Buy ($17.50) and Airbnb to Neutral; Cantor initiated Ross Stores at Overweight ($276).

items.headline: Goldman's AI memory basket is down 51% from its peak
items.summary: A sign of how hard the AI hardware complex was hit before last week's rebound; JPMorgan argues earnings still provide a buffer for now.

items.headline: On X, Wall St Engine sets the bar at $109B Nvidia revenue (+91% y/y)
items.summary: That's a touch above Nvidia's own Q3 guide of $108B ±2%; whisper numbers matter more than usual given the leadership change.

items.headline: Week ahead: retail sales & NVDA (Tue), Fed minutes (Wed), Anthropic debut + Walmart/Alibaba/PDD (Thu); PBoC LPR Nov 23, BoK Nov 26
items.summary: Also reporting: Baidu, Home Depot, Disney, JD.com, Target, Lowe's, TJX and Palo Alto Networks.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Fable 5.2 goes to all users at ~20% lower prices ($8/$40 per M tokens, 1M context) and tops an independent intelligence index; Mythos 5.2 is limited to vetted cybersecurity and life-science organisations.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon opens to paying developers and AI Ultra subscribers
items.summary: Google's most capable model, pitched at long multi-step software and security work; introductory pricing of $2/$10 per M tokens doubles on Dec 1.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen ($1.50/$7.50) and an 'Orchestrator' mode with multi-agent /swarm
items.summary: The budget model outscores its month-old flagship on some benchmarks; Orchestrator pairs Carbon as planner with Hydrogen as executor for near-Carbon results at ~24% less quota.
items.source: Rupak Ganguly / Mind and Machine Weekly

items.headline: Gemini Decision 1: a classification-only model answering 1,000 questions per pass
items.summary: Built for yes/no and multiple-choice production traffic at $0.10 per M input tokens.

items.headline: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small weights (594B MoE, 17B active, multimodal)
items.summary: Released after external red-teaming, in NVFP4 and MXFP8 checkpoints; pitched as the top open-weights model on the DesignArena web leaderboard.

items.headline: Meta ships Muse Ember 1.0, a low-cost agent model with 1M-token context
items.summary: Muse AI also gets voice calls and facial avatars, starting in the US.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts off model access to Cursor from Nov 12 after SpaceX bought the coding tool
items.summary: Earlier this month OpenAI also shipped GPT Image 2.6 (GIF support, faster generation); DevDay in September brought GPT-6.1 Sol and always-on 'Dots' agents.

items.headline: Chinese labs keep shipping: China Mobile JT-4.1 Flash (236B), Baidu ERNIE-Light-DT, Tencent Hy4, Zhipu GLM 5.3 FlashX
items.summary: Mostly cheap, long-context models priced well below US frontier APIs.

items.headline: From The Rundown: Sakana's Fugu orchestration model, SpaceX leases Colossus compute to Reflection AI, Google backs A24
items.summary: Fugu routes each request across a pool of models via one API; Reflection is renting ~$6.3B of Nvidia compute; Google put $75M behind A24 with DeepMind tooling.

items.headline: Nvidia announces GR00T 2 robot foundation model at CoRL 2026
items.summary: Plus ElevenLabs released Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live speech-to-text models.

items.headline: GitHub trending: execution infrastructure for agents, e.g. vercel-labs/agent-desktop (Rust desktop agent)
items.summary: November's trending lists tilt toward agent runtimes, scraping and desktop control rather than new model code; OpenClaw remains 2026's breakout repo.

items.headline: AI trade's two tests this week: Nvidia results (Tue) and Anthropic's Nasdaq debut (Thu)
items.summary: Anthropic reported $35.3B revenue for the 12 months to Sep 30, 2026; seven chip and cloud suppliers are taking $26B of stock at the IPO price.

items.headline: India 10Y back near 7.20% after a sharp rally to a 1-month low of 7.12%
items.summary: Profit-taking, higher US Treasury yields and heavy supply of the new 10-year paper pushed yields up again; the benchmark had touched ~7.47%, a 3-year high, in late October after the RBI hike.

items.headline: FPIs return to FAR G-secs: ~₹8,000 crore added in the first week of November
items.summary: Holdings rose from ₹3.57 to ₹3.65 lakh crore as the rupee firmed and yields eased, reversing three months of outflows.

items.headline: Street ranges for the 10Y in November: Bank of Baroda 7.25–7.35%, ICICI Bank 7.10–7.25%
items.summary: BoB sees upside risk and up to 7.75% if the RBI hikes another 50bp by March; ICICI expects softer oil and foreign buying to cap yields near term.
